inv.prod_cd: SKU, often STYLE + color like M1141 BK
inv.descrip: Item description — the current master name for this SKU
ord_log: Sales order lines (who bought which SKU)
ord_log.order_qty: Quantity sold / ordered on that line
ord_log.unit_prs: Unit price on that line. Line revenue = ORDER_QTY * UNIT_PRS
ord_log.ut_desc: Item description as recorded on the line when the order was placed. This is a historical value and can differ from inv.DESCRIP, which is the current master description. Use UT_DESC to describe what was sold at the time; join inv for the current name
ord_log.olg_dt: Order-line date, stored as an OMS day count, NOT a datetime and NOT YYYYMMDD. 81088 is 2023-01-01. Convert with DATEADD(DAY, DATEDIFF(DAY, '19000101', OLG_DT) - 81088, '20230101'); comparing this column directly against a date or calling YEAR()/MONTH()/DATEPART() on it gives wrong answers
orders.ord_amt: Order amount before fees. This is NOT the order total: total = ORD_AMT + HANDL_FEE + MISC_CHG
orders.handl_fee: Handling fee; part of the order total
orders.misc_chg: Miscellaneous charge; part of the order total
orders.ord_dt: Order date, stored as an OMS day count, NOT a datetime and NOT YYYYMMDD. 81088 is 2023-01-01. Convert with DATEADD(DAY, DATEDIFF(DAY, '19000101', ORD_DT) - 81088, '20230101'); comparing this column directly against a date or calling YEAR()/MONTH()/DATEPART() on it gives wrong answers
invoice.invs_dt: Invoice date, stored as an OMS day count, NOT a datetime and NOT YYYYMMDD. 81088 is 2023-01-01. Convert with DATEADD(DAY, DATEDIFF(DAY, '19000101', INVS_DT) - 81088, '20230101'); comparing this column directly against a date or calling YEAR()/MONTH()/DATEPART() on it gives wrong answers
plog: Purchase / container PO lines; hdl_chg=0 is ocean, hdl_chg>0 is received
plog.log_date: PO / receive date, stored as an OMS day count, NOT a datetime and NOT YYYYMMDD. 81088 is 2023-01-01. Convert with DATEADD(DAY, DATEDIFF(DAY, '19000101', LOG_DATE) - 81088, '20230101'); comparing this column directly against a date or calling YEAR()/MONTH()/DATEPART() on it gives wrong answers
bin_pur: PO bin lines with PO_QTY / RCVD_QTY

_mysql.products: Warehouse bin locations (one row per SKU + Location)
_mysql.users: Staff login accounts for this Flask app
